articles.title: “A Case Study In How To Mismanage A Young QB”: Texas Insider Rips Steve Sarkisian Over Arch Manning’s Struggles
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns have been struggling of late, barely beating Tennessee, losing two straight games, and Arch Manning has struggled to lead the offense in...
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns have been struggling of late, barely beating Tennessee, losing two straight games, and Arch Manning has struggled to lead the offense in the last few games. As a result, Manning's draft stock has taken a hit, and Texas has gone down from No. 1 to No. 19 in the AP Top 25 in just two weeks.

Now, ESPN's Pete Thamel is reporting that backup quarterback KJ Lacey Jr. has been getting more first-team quarterback reps, though he noted that Arch Manning would likely still be the QB1 but could be replaced if he continues to struggle.

With Texas struggling and Arch Manning not playing as well as expected, many are also pinning the blame on Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian. One of them is insider Graham Coffey, who blasted the Texas head coach in a very long post on social media:

"The entire Arch Manning – Texas marriage will go down as a case study in how to mismanage a young QB. If Sark crashes out this season, the last week will be a microcosm of why Texas keeps squandering super talented rosters," he wrote. "Last week he tells us Arch would be praised if he didn't have a different last name. A few days later he says Arch's job status is up for evaluation. Nobody in college football draws a wider range of headlines than Arch Manning, and his coach consistently pours gasoline on that fire."

This comes after Sarkisian defended Arch Manning after the loss against Florida, before saying that he was evaluating the quarterback's performance and not ruling out benching him. This then led to Lacey getting more first-team reps.

After his performance against then-No. 1 Ohio State during Week 2, Arch Manning became one of the favorites to be the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft. Kalshi had Manning at 31% back then, but after struggling against UTSA and Tennessee and then the two straight losses against Oklahoma and Florida, he has been plummeting steadily, according to Sports Illustrated.

In those two losses, he had a total of 433 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and two interceptions, but he also got sacked seven times. For now, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith remains the favorite as Manning continues to fall.

articles.title: How Many Rotation Spots Should Angels Allocate To Young Pitchers?
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Angels will have resources next year, which makes their rotation especially interesting.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Angels are about to have resources, which would seem to indicate an abundance of possibilities. Some kind of fast forward is going to happen in their rebuild once the ownership group of Stan Kroenke takes over after the first of the year.

One of those possibilities is about the rotation. It was an Angels' strength during the second half of the season, but it also raises an intriguing question going forward:

How many rotation spots should the Angels allocate to their group of promising young pitchers?

We already know what the top of the rotation looks like. Left-hander Reid Detmers is the ace, with rookie right-hander Walbert Urena right there with him. That means one slot is automatically allocated to a rookie, which is risky given that Urena's development next year may not be linear.

After that things get messy. Ryan Johnson certainly earned a shot at the No. 3 starter spot with a strong second half of the season, but that introduces even more risk going forward given how young Johnson is and how much of a roller coaster his brief career has been to date. Do the Halos really want to slot him in that high in the rotation?

There are veterans available to fill those last couple of spots, but that option is even messier. Yusei Kikuchi was been a reliable innings-eater for the last few years, but this year he was hurt, and Kikuchi has been the definition of mediocrity for most of his recent career. He's due $21 million in 2027. and he could easily be moved.

There's also Grayson Rodriguez, and he represents an even worse choice. He was able to make it back to the mound after an injury-plagued career, but he doesn't belong anywhere near the rotation of a team that wants to contend. The Angels would probably love to move him, but they'd be selling low given that he has absolutely no value right now.

The easy answer is to go get another veteran to go with Reid Detmers. Heck, given Kroenke's deep pockets, go get another ace. The attention would help the Halos compete with the Los Angeles Dodgers, which would be fun to watch and great for both teams.

It doesn't necessarily have to be Tarik Skubal, either. Sonny Gray will be available, and he didn't sound all that thrilled about pitching for the Boston Red Sox again. Other names will be out there and available, and the Angels should go get one of them.

articles.title: NASCAR Cup Stars Returning to JR Motorsports For Select Races in 2027
articles.summary: NASCAR Cup Series drivers Ross Chastain and Shane van Gisbergen will return to JR Motorsports to run select O’Reilly Auto Parts Series races in 2027. The Tra...
articles.body:
NASCAR Cup Series drivers Ross Chastain and Shane van Gisbergen will return to JR Motorsports to run select O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races in 2027. The Trackhouse Racing Cup Series duo will split races in the No. 9 JR Motorsports Chevrolet.Details regarding what races Chastain and van Gisbergen will be behind the wheel for have not been revealed. Chastain, a three-time O'Reilly Auto Parts Series winner, began racing part-time for JR Motorsports in 2025.SVG, a six-time O'Reilly Auto Parts Series winner, also joined JR Motorsports for a part-time slate in 2025. As announced on Tuesday, the two will be back in action for Dale Earnhardt Jr.'s team in 2027.

Ross Chastain, SVG returning to JR Motorsports in 2027

JR Motorsports' social media team broke the news of Chastain and SVG returning to the organization for "multiple" O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races next year."Back in our House and back in the No. 9 for multiple races each in 2027," via JRM on X.Chastain competed in five O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races in both 2025 and 2026 behind the wheel of the No. 9 Chevrolet. He has one victory with the organization, which came in the rain-shortened Charlotte race last May.SVG started in three O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races in 2025 and 2026. The New Zealand native posted a win at the Chicago street course in 2025 and two wins in 2026 at Circuit of The Americas and Sonoma.On the Cup side, 2026 has been a struggle for Chastain. "Melon Man" has gone winless through 33 races and failed to make the Chase for the second time in three seasons.SVG failed to make the Chase, too, as he was the first driver below the cut line at the end of the regular season. The road-course ace earned two wins this season at Watkins Glen and Sonoma.

JR Motorsports Signed Tristan McKee to Developmental Deal

In addition to bringing back two NASCAR Cup Series veterans, JR Motorsports is bringing in youth in 2027. Last Friday, it was announced that Tristan McKee, a 16-year-old developmental driver for Spire Motorsports, will compete part-time for JR Motorsports in 2027.McKee was the 2026 ARCA Menards East Series champion. The youngster out of Williamsburg, Virginia is on the fast track to climbing through NASCAR's top ranks. In a statement by the team, McKee expressed his gratitude for the opportunity with JR Motorsports."I can't wait to get started at Bristol next year with JRM. It means the world to have the opportunity to compete in one of their cars and I can't thank Dale (Earnhardt Jr.), Kelley, LW and everyone at JRM and Spire for this chance. I'm really looking forward to seeing what we can build together," McKee said.McKee will make his O'Reilly Auto Parts Series debut in the No. 9 JR Motorsports Chevrolet in the August 2027 race at Bristol. In addition, McKee will compete part-time for Spire Motorsports in the Craftsman Truck Series.McKee is a four-time winner in the ARCA Menards Series and an eight-time victor in the ARCA East Series. He won three races during the 2026 ARCA East season en route to the championship.

articles.title: How many games can Michigan win the rest of regular season if Tommy Carr is QB1?
articles.summary: Predict how many wins Michigan will have the rest of the regular season if Tommy Carr is the starting quarterback.
articles.body:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NCAA. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Michigan fans and fans across the country.

The 4-2 Michigan Wolverines made a change at quarterback at halftime last week. Tommy Carr relieved Bryce Underwood of his duties and put points on the scoreboard. Carr entered the game versus Penn State with Michigan trailing 3-0, and the Wolverines would go on to win the game 21-18. Carr was 5-of-7 for 47 yards with four carries for 36 yards and a touchdown.

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham hasn't said who will be Michigan's starting quarterback this Saturday versus Indiana, but also said there's a "secret" plan in place. Carr looked plenty good enough to warrant a start this weekend, and it seems fairly easy to predict he'll be on the field over Underwood on Saturday.

In this edition of SB Nation Reacts, we're asking how many wins Michigan will have the rest of the season if Carr is QB1. Vote below.

Here's a look at Michigan's six remaining matchups and their chances of winning each game, according to ESPN Analytics.

Oct. 24 vs. No. 6 Indiana: 17.8% chance of winning

Oct. 31 at Rutgers: 80.8% chance of winning

Nov. 7 vs. Michigan State: 77.3% chance of winning

Nov. 14 at Oregon: 18.3% chance of winning

Nov. 21 vs. UCLA: 61.7% chance of winning

Nov. 28 at Ohio State: 8.4% chance of winning

ESPN Analytics give Michigan way too low a chance versus Indiana, Oregon, and Ohio State. Oregon QB Dante Moore has been out for weeks, Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin could be out for the season, and Indiana looks more vulnerable than they did a season ago when they won the national championship. Could Michigan win out and go 10-2? Yes. Could they also lose a few of these? Yes. However, Carr could be the spark Michigan needed to make a run. There seems to be optimism that Michigan can indeed have a strong second half of the season. It'll have to start with a win on Saturday.

How did you vote this week? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Kentucky defensive spotlights in road win over Oklahoma
articles.summary: Kentucky's defense showed up on the road against Oklahoma. Here are some players that stood out and made an impact for the Wildcats defense.
articles.body:
Kentucky football moved to 6-1 and are now ranked 12th in the country after defeating Oklahoma on the road. It was impressive to see the Wildcats win a low-scoring defensive game script, which is a style of game that haven't faced all season. I thought Kentucky's defense had their best performance of the season, they were leaky at times in the first half but they really flipped the switch in the second half of this game. Here are a few defensive players that stood out and made an impact on Kentucky leaving Norman with a win.

Ty Bryant continues to find the football and be a ball hawk on the back end. Bryant is a veteran leader of this defense and he always capitalizes on errant throws. His first interception was an assist from Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace that looked like an arm punt from John Mateer. Bryant then caught the game sealing interception on a deep ball over the middle.

We spoke all offseason on how critical this experienced safety duo would be for Jay Bateman's defense, and Castell has been one of the most consistent transfers on the team this season. Castell is a sure tackler like Ty Bryant and he has ball hawking traits as well. Castell had a pass breakup in the red zone and intercepted the horribly attempted jump pass fake field goal from the Oklahoma punter. The biggest play of the game was Castell's pick six, he read the eyes of Mateer and jumped the pass to take it back to extend the lead late for Kentucky.

Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace is one of the most consistent players on this defense, he shows up every Saturday and makes big time plays. Against Oklahoma, he got a quick win on the edge and got his hand on Mateer's arm mid-release which set up an easy interception for Ty Bryant. This was a critical play as the Sooners were driving up six points, and this really swung the momentum to Kentucky's favor. Humphrey-Grace batted a ball at the line of scrimmage, he also had 1.5 sacks and 1.5 tackles for loss on Saturday.

Tavion Gadson needs to play with more consistency, but man he is dangerous on the inside when it all comes together. Gadson is one of the most underrated defensive tackles in the country and he has incredible pass rush tools for his size. He was active against Oklahoma and creating negative plays by defeating his blocks quickly against guards. Gadson finished the game with eight tackles, 1.5 sacks, 1.5 tackles for loss and he also batted a ball down at the line of scrimmage.

articles.title: Jeremy Fears Jr. returns to UConn vs MSU exhibition after injury scare
articles.summary: All-American point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. landed hard on a driving layup, grabbing at his lower left leg and foot during Michigan State's exhibition.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING - All-American point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. landed hard on a driving layup, grabbing at his lower left leg and foot during Michigan State basketball's exhibition game with Connecticut on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

The preseason national and Big Ten player of the year landed on the Huskies' Colben Landrew with 17:53 left in the second half. Fears grabbed at his left ankle and lower leg while laying on the court. He got back up and hobbled to the bench, checking himself out of the game and immediately going to the training staff.

His stay was brief. Fears received treatment and checked back into the game with 15:44 to play, with coach Tom Izzo telling him to take it easy.

That scare came after the 6-foot-2 point guard had an electric tomahawk dunk in the first half over Landrew.

articles.title: When is Tobias Harris coming back to Spurs?
articles.summary: Harris is dealing with a calf injury
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs ' big free agent signing won't be available for their season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder . Tobias Harris, who signed a two-year, $31 million deal, is out with a calf injury .

A 16-year veteran, Harris has been an effective scorer throughout his NBA career. He spent the last two seasons as a key complement to Cade Cunningham with the Detroit Pistons , averaging over 13 points and five rebounds with a 35% 3-point clip.

The Spurs are healthy outside of Harris, as the only other player who'll miss Tuesday's game is Jayden Quaintance, the rookie who's expected to sit until at least 2027.

Is Tobias Harris playing tonight vs. Thunder?

When is Tobias Harris coming back to Spurs?

Harris does not have a return date set, but Spurs coach Mitch Johnson told The Athletic , "He's ramping up. He's progressing. He still needs some more progressing on the court."

articles.title: Colin Cowherd denounces Junior Caminero’s home run trot: ‘That was obnoxious’
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Rays superstar Junior Caminero is making baseball fun again, but Colin Cowherd is the fun police. Caminero had his moment Monday night, hitting a m...
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Rays superstar Junior Caminero is making baseball fun again, but Colin Cowherd is the fun police.

Caminero had his moment Monday night, hitting a monster seventh-inning home run off Cleveland Guardians closer Cade Smith that all but punched Tampa's ticket to the World Series. The towering blast gave the Rays a 5-1 lead, and they won Game 6 of the ALCS 7-3 to advance to their third World Series in franchise history.

Perhaps more notable than the homer, however, is that Caminero took 38 seconds to round the bases. Caminero stopped several times to pose and pound his chest in celebration because, well, it was the biggest hit of his career.

Baseball purists have waved the white flag on a pitch clock; they've let the DH into the National League; they've even allowed some semblance of celebrating on the field, but Colin Cowherd and others still are not ready to see a player take 38 seconds to trot around the bases.

"I am for celebrating; I think baseball sometimes needs to lighten up," Cowherd admitted. "That is way over the top rounding first. Baseball for years was like, 'There's a way to play the game,' and everybody else had a different idea on the way to play the game. But right before he got to home plate, he stopped, I thought, 'Oh, this is obnoxious.' Two things can be true: I'm all for flexing; that was obnoxious. It's his style. He's a bit over the top, it felt obnoxious to me."

Rip players for celebrating after hitting a solo home run that made the score 8-2 in an elimination game . Mock teams for wearing goggles and popping champagne every time they clinch something . If this happened in the first inning of a June game, Cowherd would have a point. But when a home run essentially sends your team to the World Series, let the player take 38 seconds to flex.

articles.title: UND slotted at No. 6 in FCS Playoff Committee's initial Top 10
articles.summary: Oct. 20—GRAND FORKS — The UND football team received a No. 6 ranking from the FCS Playoff Committee's initial release Tuesday afternoon of the committee's To...
articles.body:
Oct. 20—GRAND FORKS — The UND football team received a No. 6 ranking from the FCS Playoff Committee's initial release Tuesday afternoon of the committee's Top 10 for the playoff bracket.

Montana State, the defending national champion, is No. 1, followed by Tarleton State, Youngstown State, Stephen F. Austin, South Dakota State and UND. Northern Arizona, South Dakota, Austin Peay and Harvard round out the Top 10.

The three other teams also receiving votes are Illinois State, Lehigh and Tennessee Tech.

The Fighting Hawks, 6-2 overall and coming off a win over then-No. 1 South Dakota State, are also ranked No. 6 in the Stats Perform FCS Top 25 media poll. UND still has to play South Dakota, Youngstown State and Illinois State this season, as well as Southern Illinois.

The official bracket release will be announced Nov. 22.

This year's FCS National championship will be played Jan. 11, 2027, at FirstBank Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee.

articles.title: Insider Reveals Michigan’s Starting QB vs. Indiana
articles.summary: Michigan is reportedly expected to start Tommy Carr over Bryce Underwood against Indiana after the freshman sparked a comeback win over Penn State.
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines appear ready to make a major change at quarterback ahead of Saturday's matchup against No. 6 Indiana. According to new reporting, true freshman Tommy Carr is expected to start against the Hoosiers , replacing Bryce Underwood following Michigan's dramatic comeback victory over Penn State.

The development comes after head coach Kyle Whittingham confirmed Monday that Michigan had selected its starting quarterback but refused to reveal the decision publicly. Now, with multiple reports pointing toward Carr, the Wolverines appear prepared to give the freshman his first collegiate start.

Tommy Carr Expected to Start Against Indiana

According to Pete Nakos' report , Carr is expected to take over as Michigan's starter Saturday. Additional reporting on the quarterback change also indicates the Wolverines are preparing to move forward with Carr while Underwood shifts into a backup role.

Carr earned the opportunity after replacing Underwood at halftime against Penn State with Michigan trailing 3-0. The freshman completed 5 of 7 passes for 47 yards while rushing for 36 yards and a touchdown, helping the Wolverines rally for a 21-18 victory.

As we previously reported , Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti had already indicated that he expected Carr to start Saturday. His assessment now appears consistent with the latest reporting surrounding Michigan's plans.

What Does This Mean for Bryce Underwood?

Underwood struggled against Penn State, completing just 5 of 11 passes for 43 yards while throwing two interceptions. His difficulties protecting the football played a major role in Whittingham's decision to make the halftime switch.

As we previously detailed following Whittingham's comments , the Michigan coaching staff wanted to evaluate both quarterbacks before choosing its starter for Indiana. That decision has apparently gone in Carr's favor, although Whittingham has not publicly confirmed the reported selection.

The freshman will face a significant challenge against an Indiana team looking to rebound from its loss to Ohio State. Carr showed promise against Penn State, but Saturday could provide a much clearer picture of his ability to lead Michigan's offense over an entire game.

For now, Tommy Carr is the reported favorite to start against Indiana, not an officially announced starter. But if the latest reports prove accurate, Michigan will enter one of its biggest games of the season with a new quarterback leading the offense.
